stem: Lisinopril belongs to which class used for high blood pressure and heart failure?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Confuses ACE inhibitors (-pril) with angiotensin receptor blockers (-sartan).
options.explanation: Angiotensin II receptor blockers such as losartan block the AT1 receptor; lisinopril instead blocks the formation of angiotensin II.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Groups every antihypertensive used in heart failure into the beta-blocker class.
options.explanation: Beta blockers such as metoprolol block beta-adrenergic receptors; lisinopril acts on the renin-angiotensin system instead.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Assumes first-line antihypertensives are all diuretics.
options.explanation: Thiazide diuretics such as hydrochlorothiazide block the distal tubule Na-Cl cotransporter; lisinopril is not a diuretic.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Places the drug at the wrong step of the renin-angiotensin cascade.
options.explanation: Direct renin inhibitors such as aliskiren block renin's conversion of angiotensinogen, one step upstream of where lisinopril acts.

options.label: E
options.misconception: None — lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor.
options.explanation: The label states that lisinopril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor; drugs ending in '-pril' share this class.

context: Learning objective: Lisinopril is in the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor class of medications.
